decisions.reason: The check-in app belongs to the firm's publicly launched passenger processing push, and its weak uptake can plausibly be blamed on the temporary COVID collapse in air travel, which is recovering in 2022, so management will persist.

PassBoard was announced with a formal home-page launch and is central to the firm's move from aviation security into passenger processing technology, so sunk investment and public commitment strongly favour keeping it as air traffic returns.

The self-service check-in solution complements the PassBoard offering, and its disappointing results can be blamed on the pandemic, so management is likely to keep it while airports reopen and automate.
